subject.title: fix(cron): keep isolated run status ok when delivery fails

question: Should successful isolated cron execution with failed post-run delivery persist as `status=ok` plus `deliveryStatus=not-delivered`, or wait for the broader first-class warning-status contract?
rationale: The code path is narrow and covered, but persisted status, backoff/alert behavior, and external consumer semantics are compatibility-sensitive and need maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve narrow split
options.body: Land this PR's `ok` plus delivery-fields behavior and direct consumers to use `deliveryStatus` or `deliveryError` for delivery failures.

options.title: Route through warning status
options.body: Pause this PR and make the broader warning-status model in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/49190 the durable public contract.

options.title: Keep current error semantics
options.body: Reject or defer the change if delivery-only failures should continue driving `status=error`, backoff, and failure alerts.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow split
recommendation.body: Land this PR's `ok` plus delivery-fields behavior and direct consumers to use `deliveryStatus` or `deliveryError` for delivery failures.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a cross-surface cron status/API decision, and the local history points to steipete for broad cron feature and delivery-dispatch ownership.
